verses.text: This is now, beloved, the second letter that I have written to you; and in both of them I stir up your sincere mind by reminding you;
that you should remember the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets, and the commandment of us, the apostles of the Lord and Savior:
knowing this first, that in the last days mockers will come, walking after their own lusts,
and saying, “Where is the promise of his coming? For, from the day that the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.”
For this they willfully forget, that there were heavens from of old, and an earth formed out of water and amid water, by the word of God;
by which means the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished.
But the heavens that now are, and the earth, by the same word have been stored up for fire, being reserved against the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men.
But don’t forget this one thing, beloved, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.
The Lord is not slow concerning his promise, as some count slowness; but is patient with us, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night; in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will be dissolved with fervent heat, and the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up.
Therefore since all these things will be destroyed like this, what kind of people ought you to be in holy living and godliness,
looking for and earnestly desiring the coming of the day of God, which will cause the burning heavens to be dissolved, and the elements will melt with fervent heat?
But, according to his promise, we look for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.
Therefore, beloved, seeing that you look for these things, be diligent to be found in peace, without defect and blameless in his sight.
Regard the patience of our Lord as salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also, according to the wisdom given to him, wrote to you;

as also in all of his letters, speaking in them of these things. In those, there are some things that are hard to understand, which the ignorant and unsettled twist, as they also do to the other Scriptures, to their own destruction.
You therefore, beloved, knowing these things beforehand, beware, lest being carried away with the error of the wicked, you fall from your own steadfastness.
But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be the glory both now and forever. Amen.

footnotes.content: Peter is tying his first letter to this one—reminding the church that his words weren't scattered thoughts but threads of the same truth. He calls them "beloved" and admits his work is to stir the embers of what they already know. Sometimes a gentle reminding is the kindest word.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The foundation is old—prophets spoke first, then the apostles passed it on. Peter is saying: don't chase after novelty. The living word has already been spoken; we hold it and pass it on as it was given.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Mockers are coming, and they walk after their own desires—that's where mockers always start. When a person decides the only truth is what serves them, mockery of anything higher follows naturally. Peter doesn't waste time on indignation; he just names it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Where is this coming?" the mockers ask. Everything stays the same, they say. But this question forgets that God has already done the impossible before—He created; He flooded; He will renew. Impatience looks like proof that nothing will change.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They choose to forget on purpose. The evidence of God's word is right there in Creation—water called forth, land established. But willful forgetting is the luxury of those who want to live as if no one is watching.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Flood is the historical anchor Peter returns to: God *did* act decisively before. The world perished by water. No doctrine here—just historical fact. If you read Genesis and Noah's day, you know God is not indifferent to human rebellion.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fire is coming next, Peter says, just as surely as water came before. The earth is stored up, reserved—a word suggesting deliberate provision, not accident. This isn't threat; it's clarity. The Lord has already decided.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Don't forget this one thing." A thousand years, a day—it's Peter's way of saying your impatience is measured in a time He doesn't keep. The Lord's delays aren't hesitation. They're mercy working on a calendar we don't see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here's the heart of it: the Lord is patient because He doesn't wish that any perish. Not slowness or weakness—patient love. Every day He waits is an invitation to turn back. The delay itself is the gospel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Like a thief—suddenly, when least expected. Elements dissolve, earth burned. It's not poetry; it's promise. Peter is preparing people to hold lightly to this world without despair, because he knows what comes next.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "What kind of people?" The question that haunts and redeems. If all will be shaken, then how should I live *today*? Holiness and godliness aren't rules; they're the only reasonable response to eternity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Earnestly desiring—Peter's readers are not cowering in fear but *longing* for the day when God makes all things new. There's a holy eagerness here: the pain of this age makes the promise precious.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "According to his promise." Not guessing, not hoping blindly—the promise was spoken. New heavens, new earth, and righteousness dwells there. The old corruption burned away, and in its place, what was always meant to be.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Diligent, blameless, at peace—Peter calls us to readiness not through anxiety but through nearness to Christ. When you live looking toward Him, you find yourself becoming what you were made for.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Paul wrote hard things too, Peter acknowledges. Even his beloved brother's letters press toward the End. Peter calls this God's patience, His salvation at work. The hard word and the kind word both serve the same mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peter speaks of Paul's letters as Scripture—already, in his own day. And he warns: some twist even this to their destruction. Truth twisted is a stumbling block. Read carefully, with reverence for what you hold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Beware, beloved." Not in anger but as a shepherd. Peter knows the seduction of error—how smoothly it slides in when you're unsettled. Steadfastness is the anchor. Hold to what you have been given.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Grow in grace and knowledge of Jesus—Peter's last word is an invitation to depth, not merely survival. Readers today hear an echo in this: even now, as we wait, we are not static but becoming. His grace meets us where we are, and knowledge of Him shapes us into His likeness.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
